title: Parallel Work and Cancellation
summary: Using several cores and stopping work politely - Task.Run for CPU-bound work, Parallel.For and Parallel.ForEachAsync, limiting concurrency with SemaphoreSlim, thread safety with lock, Interlocked and concurrent collections, CancellationToken and CancellationTokenSource, timeouts, and progress reporting.

cards.q: Why can count++ from several threads give a total that is too low?
cards.a:
count++ reads, adds and writes in separate steps, so two threads can read the same old value

If two threads both read 7 and both write 8, one increment is lost. `Interlocked.Increment` or a lock makes the step atomic.

cards.q: Who creates the CancellationTokenSource and who checks the token?
cards.a:
The caller creates and cancels the source; the worker receives the token and checks it

Cancellation is cooperative: nothing stops the worker unless it checks the token (or passes it to methods that do).

cards.q: Which is the right tool to run a heavy calculation without freezing a desktop app's window?
cards.a:
await Task.Run(() => Calculate())

An async method still runs its CPU work on the calling thread; Task.Run moves it to the thread pool.
